title: Indrāṇī, whose husband does not age

words.role: the set in which she is named

words.meaning: she who has a good husband

sandhi.rule: i before a dissimilar vowel becomes y
m before c is written as the palatal nasal ñ (or anusvāra)

morphology.note: Vedic short i for नारीषु (Bhāskara: «छान्दसं ह्रस्वत्वम्»).
√mṛ ‘die’ inflected as a thematic middle (Bhāskara: «व्यत्ययेन शप्»); classical म्रियते.

translation.literal: Indrāṇī, among these women, I have heard [to be] the one with a good husband; for her husband never at all dies of old age.
translation.readable: Of all women, I have heard, Indrāṇī is the most fortunate in her husband, for he never grows old and dies.

meaning: A verse praising Indrāṇī, the wife of Indra: among all women she is the one whose husband is best, for Indra never ages and never dies. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (1.7.13.1) it is the puronuvākyā of an offering of rice to Indrāṇī, made — Bhāskara says — for one whose army lacks spirit; Bhāskara’s gloss ends by asking that Indrāṇī make that army eager. The verse also stands in the Ṛgveda (10.86.11), in the dialogue hymn of Indra, Indrāṇī and Vṛṣākapi, with a different second word (subhagām for supatnīm) and the refrain viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ. The use of the verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition, not to the Veda: in its source it serves another rite (see the commentary).
in_the_rite: The second mantra of Śukra’s step in the Navagraha sūktam, addressed to Indrāṇī. S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together in the salutation that follows, without saying which mantra is whose.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The setting in the Saṃhitā, from Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara’s viniyoga: «इन्द्राण्यै चरुं निर्वपेद्यस्य सेनाऽसंशितेव स्यात्» — the verse is its puronuvākyā («इन्द्राणीमित्यनुष्टुप्»).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: «सुपत्नीं शोभनपतिकाम्»; «न ह्यस्याः पतिः जरसा वयोहान्या मरते म्रियते»; and the prayer behind it: «सैव महाभागा इन्द्राणी अस्मत्सेनामुत्साहवतीं करोत्वित्यर्थः».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Metre anuṣṭubh (Bhāskara). The Ṛgveda (10.86.11) reads सुभगाम् for सुपत्नीम् and adds the refrain विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः.
